channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President proposes climate integration initiative at COP31 summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed a climate integration initiative at the COP31 World Leaders Summit in Antalya. He highlighted Uzbekistan's commitment to climate action, noting a 35% reduction in emissions per GDP unit and a new target of 50% by 2035. The President also detailed progress in water conservation and increasing green energy.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Expand Trade and Economic Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate Chairperson met with the President of the Korea Importers Association to discuss developing trade and economic ties. Discussions focused on exporting Uzbek products, particularly agricultural goods, to the Korean market and exploring a free trade agreement to boost bilateral trade. The importance of strengthening business ties and establishing joint ventures was emphasized.

item.title: Turkmenistan's TAPI Gas Pipeline Reaches Vicinity of Herat, Afghanistan
item.description: Turkmenistan announced its TAPI gas pipeline has reached the outskirts of Herat, Afghanistan. The first Afghan section is slated for completion by late 2026. Satellite imagery confirms pipeline construction approximately 22 kilometers west of Herat.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Major Production Complex for High-Voltage Electrical Equipment
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched a new high-tech production complex, 'NURA Electric,' in the Tashkent region, specializing in high and low-voltage electrical equipment. The facility aims to reduce import reliance, producing over 1,500 types of products with a 60% localization rate.

item.title: Uzbekistan Promotes Central Asian Integration Amid Climate Challenges
item.description: Uzbekistan is advocating for strengthened regional cooperation to address climate change impacts on water resources, agriculture, energy, and security. The nation emphasizes trust-based approaches, experience sharing, and joint initiatives. Climate integration, population protection, technological cooperation, and climate finance access were key topics at the COP31 session attended by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Ties with US Through Youth Educational Programs
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing its international relations by fostering educational exchanges with the United States. A meeting in Washington focused on developing youth connections and organizing short-term educational programs for Uzbek students. Discussions included visits to leading universities and tech companies, aiming to broaden students' horizons in education, technology, and entrepreneurship.

item.title: US Exim Bank and DFC Decline Financing for Kazakhstan Tungsten Project
item.description: The US Export-Import Bank (EXIM) and the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) will not finance the Cove Kaz Capital Group's tungsten project in Kazakhstan. Bloomberg reports that Washington doubts the mines can be launched on schedule and fears proximity to China and Russia. Political disputes surrounding the Trump family's investments are also a factor.

item.title: Book on Mirziyoyev's Doctrine Launched in Seoul During Uzbek Delegation Visit
item.description: A Korean edition of the book "Mirziyoyev's Doctrine: Diplomacy of Opportunities in an Era of Global Instability" was presented in Seoul. The event, attended by Korean academics and business figures, highlighted Uzbekistan's reforms and foreign policy under President Mirziyoyev. The book covers Uzbekistan's foreign policy principles, regional cooperation, and international economic ties.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Attends COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov is attending the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change in Antalya, Turkey, on the President's instructions. The summit discusses global cooperation on sustainable development and climate change. Bektenov highlighted Kazakhstan's 'Clean Kazakhstan' initiative and afforestation efforts.

item.title: Central Asian nations seek to finalize business deals at Washington summit
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan sent high-level delegations to the B20 business summit in Washington, signaling a strong desire to finalize agreements with American businesses. Both nations expressed eagerness to move beyond rhetoric to concrete projects and mutually beneficial partnerships.

item.title: Turkmenistan Hosts International Investment Forum with Global Participation
item.description: Turkmenistan held an international investment forum in Ashgabat, attracting participants from Central Asia, the USA, UK, Japan, Singapore, Saudi Arabia, Germany, China, and France. The event focused on analyzing international standards for reducing methane emissions and improving the legal framework for the energy sector, aligning with national development priorities and the country's 'open door' policy.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Climate Integration Model for Central Asia
item.description: Uzbekistan has put forward an initiative to develop a Climate Integration Model for Central Asia. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced this at COP31, emphasizing that no single country can solve climate issues alone. He proposed three key areas for cooperation: information exchange, technological solutions, and financial mechanisms.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes New Climate Cooperation Model for Central Asia
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has proposed a new model for cooperation in Central Asia to combat climate risks. The initiative includes exchanging climate-related data, promoting green technologies, and developing new financial support mechanisms for the region.

item.title: UK to Tighten Measures Against Forced Labor, Affecting Turkmenistan
item.description: The UK government will implement a law requiring due diligence on human rights in supply chains, banning goods produced with forced labor. These measures, similar to those in the US and EU, could impact Turkmenistan's cotton exports. A Swiss NGO highlighted the involvement of Swiss textile machinery suppliers in Turkmenistan's forced labor system.

item.title: Kazakh President Attends CSTO Security Council Meeting in Moscow
item.description: The head of state of Kazakhstan participated in a session of the Collective Security Council of the CSTO in Moscow. The meeting focused on security matters within the organization.

item.title: Turkmenistan's National Leader Attends COP31 Leaders Summit in Turkey
item.description: Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow, Chairman of the Halk Maslahaty of Turkmenistan, attended the Leaders Summit within COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. The summit addressed global issues including food security, agriculture, health, energy, transport, trade, finance, science, industry, and sustainable urban development, focusing on strengthening national commitments to climate change mitigation.

item.title: Turkmenistan's National Leader Addresses UN Climate Change Conference in Turkey
item.description: Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow, Chairman of the Halk Maslahaty of Turkmenistan, delivered a speech at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Turkey. He expressed gratitude for the invitation and hospitality, emphasizing Turkmenistan's commitment to international climate agreements, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and enhancing energy efficiency through modern technologies and national strategies.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Meets Russian President Vladimir Putin
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on November 11. Japarov expressed gratitude for the warm reception and Putin's attention to developing Kyrgyz-Russian relations, noting the role of trust and dialogue. Putin affirmed readiness to expand cooperation.

item.title: Iran Threatens to Target US Bases, Near and Far, if Attacked Again
item.description: Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary stated that if the US attacks Iran again, it will target both near and distant US bases, potentially including military installations in Europe. This threat aims to impose costs on the US for any aggression against Iran.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Urges International Partners to Support Issyk-Kul Preservation Initiative
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Prime Minister urged international development institutions, donor countries, and the private sector to support the initiative to preserve Lake Issyk-Kul. He announced Kyrgyzstan's commitment of $10 million to a newly established international trust fund for the lake's protection.

item.title: Turkmenistan Enhances Climate Change Reporting Capabilities with FAO Support
item.description: Turkmenistan's Ministry of Environment Protection, in collaboration with the FAO, held a workshop on strengthening national capacities for fulfilling the Enhanced Transparency Framework requirements under the Paris Agreement. The event highlighted Turkmenistan's commitment to climate action, international cooperation, and sustainable development, emphasizing the importance of transparency in climate reporting.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Prioritizes Aviation Infrastructure for Tourism Growth
item.description: Improving aviation and airport infrastructure is crucial for developing tourism in Kyrgyzstan, according to Manasbek Samidinov, head of "Kyrgyzstan Airports" OJSC. He stated that air travel is the primary transport for tourists due to the country's geography and underdeveloped rail network. Enhancing airport capacity is essential to handle increasing passenger flow.

item.title: Taliban Interior Minister Meets Russian Special Representative on Counter-Narcotics
item.description: Sirajuddin Haqqani, the Taliban's interior minister, met with Zamir Kabulov, Russia's special representative. They discussed counter-narcotics efforts and regional developments. The Taliban's stance on a UN report concerning drugs in Afghanistan was also raised. Kabulov reportedly praised the Taliban's efforts in combating narcotics.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Holds Key Meetings in Antalya, Including with Bangladesh PM and UN Officials
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held several important meetings in Antalya, Turkey, on the sidelines of COP31. He met with Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Executive Secretary of the UN Convention to Combat Desertification, Ibrahim Thiaw, and UNDP Administrator Achim Steiner. Discussions focused on bilateral cooperation and climate change issues.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Invites Global Leaders to Second Global Mountain Summit in Bishkek in 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Prime Minister, Adylbek Kasymaliev, invited all delegation heads to the Second Global Mountain Summit to be held in Bishkek in October 2027. He also called for support for the UN's "Decade of Action for Mountains" (2028–2037) and proposed establishing a center for mountain resilience.

item.title: Mountain Countries Need $187 Billion Annually for Climate Adaptation, Official States
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Cabinet of Ministers Adylbek Kasymaliev stated that mountain countries require nearly $187 billion annually for climate adaptation measures. He noted that current international support amounts to only $13.8 billion. Kasymaliev called for reforming the international financial architecture to ease access to climate finance for developing nations.

item.title: Unemployed Afghan Women Struggle to Meet Basic Needs Amidst Economic Hardship
item.description: Unemployed women in Afghanistan report an inability to afford basic necessities like new clothing or replace worn-out household items. Many, like a former government employee and widow, are forced to reuse old clothes and wash laundry by hand due to broken appliances and lack of funds. This economic distress affects single mothers and former NGO workers alike, impacting their ability to purchase even essential hygiene products.

item.title: Unemployment and High Dowry Force Afghan Youth to Postpone Marriage
item.description: Unemployment, poverty, and traditional customs are preventing many young Afghans from marrying. A 39-year-old man cites job scarcity and economic instability as reasons for remaining single, fearing future difficulties if he marries without financial preparation. Additionally, the high dowry, often seven to eight hundred thousand Afghanis, is a significant barrier, leading some to undertake arduous journeys for work to meet these financial demands.

item.title: Tajik President's Moscow Visit: Regional Issues and Migrant Rights Discussed
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon's visit to Moscow is highlighted, with discussions reportedly covering the reasons for his trip and a dispute in Jayhun. The news also mentions calls for supporting the rights of Tajik activists and reports that migrants are being deprived of the right to drive taxis. The broadcast covers various segments including politics, economy, and regional news.

item.title: Amnesty International Launches Global Campaign Against Gender Apartheid in Afghanistan
item.description: Amnesty International has launched a global campaign, '16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence,' to highlight gender apartheid in Afghanistan to international decision-makers. The campaign, running from November 25 to December 10, aims to raise public awareness and urge action, as Afghanistan has fallen off the media and political radar due to recent global crises. Amnesty calls for support to ensure Afghan women and girls are not forgotten.

item.title: UN Warns Central Asian Nations as Afghanistan's Opium Production Surges Fivefold
item.description: Opium production in Afghanistan has surged fivefold to 1,466 tons, with poppy cultivation expanding by 325% to 43,300 hectares. The UN Office on Drugs and Crime warned in Tashkent that the shift of cultivation towards Central Asian borders increases the risk of drug smuggling through Uzbekistan and neighboring countries.

item.title: Taliban Block Kabul Roads Leading to Loya Jirga Hall Amidst Major Meeting
item.description: Sources report the Taliban have imposed strict security measures and blocked roads leading to the Loya Jirga Hall in Kabul for a significant meeting. Details regarding the meeting's agenda, participants, or objectives remain undisclosed. Traffic disruptions have been reported in the city.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan to Enhance Cooperation in Mountain Ecosystem Preservation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan will strengthen cooperation in preserving mountain ecosystems. Ministers met on the sidelines of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) to discuss joint efforts, biodiversity conservation, and the snow leopard population. Collaboration will focus on monitoring, data exchange, and anti-poaching.

item.title: UN Women: Climate Crisis Disproportionately Affects Women and Girls
item.description: UN Women reports that women and girls bear a greater burden from the climate crisis, facing a 34% greater income loss than men for each degree Celsius rise in global temperature. The organization urges governments to center gender equality in climate policies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Supports Green Industrialization and Food Security at COP31 Leaders Summit
item.description: Kyrgyzstan backs priorities like green industrialization, food security, sustainable healthcare, and clean energy transition at the COP31 Leaders Summit. Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev highlighted the country's practical steps in developing hydropower and renewable energy sources. He noted the significant gap in climate finance, with annual needs for adaptation in mountainous countries reaching $187 billion, while actual international support is only $13.8 billion.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks Seventh Globally for Affordable Mobile Internet Among 55 Countries
item.description: Kazakhstan has secured seventh place for the affordability of mobile internet among 55 countries with high connection speeds, according to an analysis cited by the Ministry of Digital Development. One gigabyte of mobile data costs approximately $0.30, significantly lower than the global average of $1.23. The average monthly fee is around $10.65, substantially less than the over $27 in developed nations.

item.title: Uzbek Scientists Study Population Genomics and Tissue Regeneration Methods
item.description: Scientists in Uzbekistan are studying population genomics and seeking ways to regenerate damaged tissues at the Center of Advanced Technologies. Projects investigate DNA, observe living cells, and develop biological preparations to understand disease mechanisms and explore new treatment avenues.

item.title: Kazakh President Saparov Meets with Russian President Putin to Discuss Bilateral Relations
item.description: Kazakh President Saparov met with Russian President Putin during a working visit to Russia. They discussed deepening strategic partnership, expanding trade and economic cooperation, and collaboration in energy, industry, finance, and education. Both leaders expressed commitment to strengthening bilateral ties through joint initiatives.

item.title: Tajikistan to Assume Chairmanship of CSTO in 2027
item.description: Tajikistan will assume the rotating chairmanship of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) in 2027. President Emomali Rahmon stated that Dushanbe aims to focus on strengthening regional security during its tenure. This comes as the CSTO addresses concerns regarding potential armed group incursions and drug trafficking from Afghanistan.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva meets French President Macron in Paris
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration, met with French President Emmanuel Macron in Paris. They discussed expanding bilateral strategic partnership in defense, security, cyber technologies, and AI, as well as joint economic and humanitarian initiatives. Mirziyoyeva highlighted shared concerns on child welfare.
